beschreibung: The conversation is the central tool of all counseling. This module introduces the client-centered core attitudes according to Carl Rogers and trains the basic techniques of active listening, paraphrasing, reflecting emotional content, and purposeful questioning. Building on this, you will become acquainted with motivational interviewing and structure a counseling process from first contact through the contract to its conclusion – practiced in several conversation simulations.
lernziele: You can explain the client-centered core attitudes of empathy, unconditional positive regard, and congruence and recognize them in conversation examples.
You can use and distinguish paraphrasing and reflecting emotional content in a targeted way.
You can use open and closed questions appropriately for the situation and avoid typical questioning pitfalls.
You can apply the spirit, the OARS techniques, and the handling of ambivalence and change talk in motivational interviewing.
You can structure a counseling process in phases and agree on a counseling contract transparently.

pruefung.frage: Which three core attitudes did Carl Rogers describe for the counselor? (Multiple answers possible)
optionen: Empathy
Confrontation
Unconditional positive regard
Congruence
Neutrality
pruefung.erklaerung: Rogers named empathic understanding, unconditional positive regard, and congruence (genuineness). Confrontation contradicts the approach; neutrality is a term from other schools, especially the systemic and psychodynamic traditions.

pruefung.frage: A client says: “Since the separation, I sit alone in the apartment in the evenings and stare at the wall.” Which response reflects emotional content?
optionen: “Since the separation, you have been spending your evenings alone at home.”
“Why don’t you do something with friends?”
“It sounds as if you feel very lonely and empty.”
“That will pass; after a separation this is normal.”
pruefung.erklaerung: The third response names the underlying feeling. The first is a paraphrase of the content, the second a why-question with implicit advice, the fourth reassurance and thus a communication roadblock.

pruefung.aussage: Closed questions should always be avoided in counseling.
pruefung.erklaerung: Closed questions are useful for clarifying facts, bringing about decisions, or making targeted assessments in crises, for example when asking about suicidal thoughts. What is problematic is their excessive or unreflective use.

pruefung.frage: What does the acronym OARS stand for in motivational interviewing?
optionen: Open questions, affirmations, reflections (reflective listening), summaries
Orientation, analysis, resources, strategies
Ordering, assessing, reflecting, steering
Openness, acceptance, respect, self-determination
pruefung.erklaerung: OARS stands for open questions, affirmations, reflections, and summaries. These basic techniques serve to build the relationship and to evoke change talk.

pruefung.frage: Which statements are change talk? (Multiple answers possible)
optionen: “I want to spend more time with my children again.”
“Smoking is the only thing that relaxes me.”
“I think I could manage to stay away from the gambling hall.”
“Last week I went without wine twice.”
“I see no reason at all to change anything.”
pruefung.erklaerung: Desire, ability, and first steps are forms of change talk (DARN-CAT). The other two statements are sustain talk, that is, statements in favor of the status quo.

pruefung.frage: What do Miller and Rollnick call the “righting reflex”?
optionen: The tendency of clients to conceal relapses
The impulse of helpers to correct problems immediately and to argue for change
A technique for converting sustain talk into change talk
The client’s automatic correction of inaccurate paraphrases
pruefung.erklaerung: The righting reflex is the well-meant urge to set things right. With ambivalent people, it often leads them to argue the other side. MI therefore practices holding this reflex back.

pruefung.aussage: The counseling contract should also make the limits of confidentiality transparent.
pruefung.erklaerung: Transparency about confidentiality and its limits, for example in the case of acute danger to oneself or others or endangerment of a child’s welfare, is part of a fair and sustainable contract.

pruefung.frage: A mother says: “The youth welfare office sent me.” In terms of clarifying the mandate, what does this statement describe?
optionen: The concern
The mandate
The contract
The occasion
pruefung.erklaerung: The statement names the external trigger, that is, the occasion. The mother’s own concern and her concrete mandate to the counseling service still have to be clarified before a contract can be concluded.
